title: Hanamaki — 花巻
goal: Formally study a flower character met earlier, travel with a friend, and describe a short visit in the past.

blocks.text: 花巻
はなまき — Hanamaki

Hanamaki is associated with hot springs and the writer Miyazawa Kenji. The cultural context supports a quiet journey-with-a-friend scene; the story below is our own fictional learner story, not a retelling of his work.

**花巻に行きます。**
はなまきに いきます。
I go / will go to Hanamaki.
The first character is one you encountered around Hirosaki's blossoms. The hot-spring word connects back to Noboribetsu. Two earlier parts of the Journey meet in one new location.

items: **Kanji:** 花 · **Useful meaning/readings:** flower; はな; on カ · **Radical and components:** Radical 艹, くさかんむり, the grass/plant top. 化 below supplies a historical sound element · **Learning role:** Core. The plant top is a meaning clue; it does not tell us the full name reading.

**Kanji:** 巻 · **Useful meaning/readings:** roll; wind; まく/まき; on カン · **Radical and components:** Historical indexing family 卩/㔾, ふしづくり/まげわりふ; some dictionaries classify modern 巻 under 己, おのれ. Modern upper 龹-like strokes and lower 己-shaped curl are recognition chunks · **Learning role:** Encounter. Compare the lower 㔾-like part in older 卷 with the 己-shaped part in modern 巻. Dictionary indexing can follow history or the modern shape. Neither approach means “self” explains every use of 巻; do not read the city name by adding component glosses.

blocks.text: **花巻 / はなまき**. This spelling gives us useful kanji to inspect, but “flower roll” is not a verified etymology of Hanamaki's name.
化 is visible inside 花, with 亻 and 匕 shapes. Those are helpful nested recognition pieces. We are not teaching that the “person + spoon” English meanings produce the meaning “flower.”

cards.title: 花 Returns as a Studied Character

blocks.text:
**花** — はな — flower.
**花見** — はなみ — flower viewing, especially cherry-blossom viewing in the customary expression.
You first encountered 花 with the Hirosaki park scene. Now study it deliberately. **花 + 見** combines today's flower character with 見 from Hokkaido.

**公園で花を見ます。**
こうえんで はなを みます。
I look at flowers in the park.

**花見に行きます。**
はなみに いきます。
I go to view the blossoms.
The examples are possible practice activities, not a claim that every Hanamaki park always has flowering cherry trees. Seeing 花 in a name also does not mean the location is defined only by flowers.

**友だち** — ともだち — friend.
**友** — とも; common on reading ユウ.

友 is indexed under **又**, また. The modern upper-left hand-like shape and lower 又 can be recognised together. A “hands connecting” mnemonic helps remember friendship; do not treat every modern component gloss as a literal definition of every word using 友.

**友だちがいます。**
ともだちが います。
I have a friend / there is a friend.

Existence wording can express having someone in your life in the appropriate context. In a map scene the same words may mean a friend is present there. Read the context rather than assigning one rigid English phrase to います.
**私** — わたし — I; me.

私 uses **禾**, のぎへん when on the left, as its radical, and **厶** on the right. Recognise the shapes; their visible grain/private associations are not a simple explanation of how the everyday pronoun means “I.” 厶 is a shape you saw in 弘, but a shared shape does not force a shared reading or semantic role.

**私は青森に行きました。**
わたしは あおもりに いきました。
I went to Aomori.
Japanese often omits 私 when it is clear who is speaking. **青森に行きました** can already mean “I went to Aomori” in a personal account. Do not insert 私 into every sentence simply because English needs “I.”
**私の本** — わたしの ほん — my book. This reuses の to express a relationship/possession.

You learned **りんごと水**: apples **and** water.
Now learn **友だちと**: **with** a friend.

**友だちと花巻に行きます。**
ともだちと はなまきに いきます。
I go / will go to Hanamaki with a friend.

**友だちと魚を食べます。**
ともだちと さかなを たべます。
I eat fish with a friend.
と marks the companion in the action. The object of eating still uses を, and the destination still uses に.
Contrast **私と友だち** (me and my friend, a joined noun phrase) with **友だちと行きます** (go with my friend). The same particle has two related uses; its surrounding words tell us which use is active.

**会う** — あう — meet.
**会います** — あいます — meet / will meet.

会 is indexed under **人**, ひと. Its modern upper 人-like shape and lower 云-shaped section help distinguish it from other characters. The lower shape is not an instruction to translate the word as “cloud.” Our goal is to recognise 会 in a useful verb.

**友だちに会います。**
ともだちに あいます。
I meet / will meet a friend.

With this verb, **に marks the person you meet**. In the companion sentence **友だちと行きます**, と marks the person who accompanies you. For our beginner examples, practise this distinction without claiming that 会う can never occur with と in other constructions.

**九時に公園で友だちに会います。**
くじに こうえんで ともだちに あいます。
I meet a friend in the park at nine.
Breakdown:

items: 九時に — at nine: time.
公園で — in the park: place of the meeting action.
友だちに — a friend: the person met.
会います — meet.

blocks.text: The repeated に is not a mistake. Its jobs differ because the words before it differ.
Do not memorise only the whole string. Change 九時 to 九時半. Then change 公園 to 店. Each change reuses a component of knowledge introduced earlier in the Journey.
**誰** — だれ — who? The word is core; the character is assisted.

**誰と行きますか。**
だれと いきますか。
Who will you go with?

**友だちと行きます。**
ともだちと いきます。
I will go with a friend.

**私と友だちは二人です。**
わたしと ともだちは ふたりです。
My friend and I make two people.
The と in 私と友だち joins nouns. 二人 is read ふたり, just as in Hachinohe. The personal account adds perspective without replacing the counting system.

items: **Japanese:** 会います · **Reading:** あいます · **Meaning:** meet / will meet
**Japanese:** 会いません · **Reading:** あいません · **Meaning:** do not / will not meet
**Japanese:** 会いました · **Reading:** あいました · **Meaning:** met
**Japanese:** 会いませんでした · **Reading:** あいませんでした · **Meaning:** did not meet

blocks.text:
**昨日、友だちに会いました。**
きのう、ともだちに あいました。
Yesterday, I met a friend.
The character 会 stays the same. You learned this four-part polite pattern through 行く in Noboribetsu. Reusing it with another verb helps it become a real pattern rather than four isolated flashcards.

**今日は会いません。**
きょうは あいません。
I will not meet [them] today.
The omitted person can be understood from the previous sentence. Negative nonpast and negative past mean different things; keep the time word in view.

**昨日、友だちと花巻に行きました。**
きのう、ともだちと はなまきに いきました。
Yesterday, I went to Hanamaki with a friend.

**花巻に温泉があります。**
はなまきに おんせんが あります。
There are hot springs in Hanamaki.

**私たちは温泉に入りました。そして、休みました。**
わたしたちは おんせんに はいりました。そして、やすみました。
We entered a hot spring. Then we rested.

私たち / わたしたち means we; the -たち group expression is an assisted encounter rather than a new general plural rule. Entering a hot spring uses に. Resting uses a familiar polite past. This fictional story deliberately returns to Noboribetsu vocabulary.

cards.title: Practice: A Friend and a Journey

blocks.text: **Practice:**

items: Complete “with a friend”: 友だち＿＿行きます。 A. と / B. を / C. で.
Complete the taught meeting pattern: 友だち＿＿会います。 A. を / B. に / C. で.
Which means “did not meet”? 会いません / 会いませんでした.
Which earlier lesson first previewed 花 in this manuscript?

blocks.text: **Answers:** 1 と: companion. 2 に: person met in this pattern. 3 会いませんでした. 4 Hirosaki, with blossoms/flowers.

items: 花巻 = はなまき; 花 is now studied, 巻 remains encounter.
花/はな → 花見/はなみ; 艹 is the plant radical.
友だち = ともだち; 私 = わたし; 会う = あう.
友だちと行きます versus 友だちに会います.
九時に公園で友だちに会います: time / action location / person met.
誰と行きますか; 二人 = ふたり.
会いました and 会いませんでした reuse Hokkaido's verb endings.
温泉 and entering/resting tie the new lesson back to Hokkaido.

blocks.text: **Iwate's three location lessons are complete. Continue to the Iwate Reading Journey and test. The next prefecture is Miyagi / 宮城.**
